question: Should OpenClaw start rejecting unsafe integer byte-size values in config and exported helper paths now, even if existing unrepresentable numeric thresholds stop validating or fall back to defaults?
rationale: Repository policy treats stricter config validation and plugin-facing helper behavior as compatibility-sensitive, and this PR deliberately changes how existing unsafe numeric values are handled.

options.title: Accept strict unsafe-size rejection
options.body: Treat unsafe integer byte-size values as corrupted input and land the narrow fix after exact-head checks pass.

options.title: Require upgrade note first
options.body: Ask for PR-body or release-note context telling users to replace unsafe numeric thresholds with safe integer or string byte-size values.

options.title: Pause for migration policy
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers consider existing unsafe numeric thresholds a shipped config contract that needs doctor or migration handling.

recommendation.title: Accept strict unsafe-size rejection
recommendation.body: Treat unsafe integer byte-size values as corrupted input and land the narrow fix after exact-head checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the clearest current merge/release routing candidate for accepting a config-validation compatibility tradeoff on this recently introduced surface.
